title: BubbleGrade, grading bubbles by sound
caption: It turns Doppler heart sound into pictures, scores each slice for bubbles, then averages.
alt: Architecture diagram of BubbleGrade, 7.2 million parameters, read in three columns. Left, bottom to top: a 5-second slice of Doppler heart sound at 16 kHz, a Fourier transform with a 25 ms window and a 10 ms hop, then 64 mel bands, a log and subtraction of the slice mean, giving a log-mel picture of 64 bands by 498 time steps. Middle, top to bottom, a MobileNetV4-Conv-Medium network that started from ImageNet weights and was fine-tuned: a 3 by 3 convolution with stride 2 (32 channels), 3 MobileNetV4 blocks (80 channels, an 8 by 63 grid), 8 blocks (160 channels, 4 by 32), 11 blocks (256 channels, 2 by 16) and a 1 by 1 convolution to 960 channels. Right, bottom to top: a 1 by 1 convolution gives one bubble score per 0.3-second cell, the 16-cell bubble map; their mean is the slice score s; an ordinal output turns s into the chances that the grade is at least I, II, III and IV, P(grade at least k) = sigmoid(s + b_k), here 0.98, 0.95, 0.86 and 0.23 for the slice shown; the chances are averaged over the clip's 12 slices, taken 1 second apart, the last one aligned to the clip's end. Output for this held-out clip: grade III, alert on, because the mean chance of grade III or more, 0.78, is above the alert threshold 0.085. A technician graded the same clip III. The three pictures are real: the slice's loudness, the log-mel picture the model computed and its bubble map. Marked AI-generated diagram.
